skill.name: webask-integration-triage
skill.description: Находит причину, по которой ответы на опрос WebAsk не доходят до внешней системы, и устраняет её. Применяется, когда человек сообщает, что заявки не приходят в CRM, уведомления не появляются в Telegram или MAX, строки не добавляются в Google Таблицу либо не срабатывает вебхук.
skill.summary: Diagnose WebAsk integration failures, explain required repairs, and retry supported deliveries after the cause is resolved.
skill.author: webaskio

finding_verdicts.reason: The parent-directory sequences appear in HTML breadcrumb links to repository documentation. They do not perform filesystem operations or process attacker-controlled paths.
Backticks format the get_quiz_list MCP tool name in Markdown. The instruction identifies and confirms a survey, without invoking a shell.
The heading formats get_quiz_integrations as inline code. It describes reading integration status through MCP, not executing shell commands.
The backticks delimit the blocked_by_tariff status value in a Markdown table. The instruction says to explain the restriction and stop.
The backticks delimit the not_connected status value, not executable content. The user must connect the account through the dashboard.
The backticks format the disabled status value in a Markdown table. The associated instruction explicitly requires consent before enabling delivery.
The inline code names get_integration_logs for reading Telegram and MAX delivery errors. No shell execution or command interpolation is present.
The Markdown names manage_quiz_crm, with the check action specified on the next line. This is a documented connectivity check, not shell execution.
Backticks format the check action for the CRM MCP tool. Contacting the configured CRM portal is part of the requested diagnosis, not a shell command.
The backticks name manage_quiz_google_sheets and its show action. The instruction inspects the existing integration and contains no shell execution.
The inline code names the resend_integration_logs MCP tool, not a shell command. Retries serve the stated recovery workflow and follow correction of the failure.
The backticks format get_quiz_webhooks and get_quiz_webhook_logs as MCP tool identifiers. Both instructions inspect configured webhooks or delivery logs, without shell execution.
The backticks format resend_quiz_webhook_log, a documented webhook retry operation. The surrounding workflow limits retries to recovery and warns against exposing or overwriting secret headers.

content.value_statement: Missing survey deliveries can leave teams without leads, notifications, or spreadsheet updates. This skill guides status checks, service-specific diagnosis, and supported retries after repairs.
actual_capabilities: Find a survey by name and confirm its identity before making changes.
Distinguish plan restrictions, missing connections, and disabled delivery through integration status checks.
Read Telegram and MAX delivery logs to identify service errors and pending retries.
Check Bitrix24 connectivity and inspect Google Sheets integration settings.
Inspect webhook configuration and delivery response codes without requesting masked header secrets.
Retry supported messenger deliveries or individual webhook deliveries after the underlying problem is resolved.
limitations: Requires configured WebAsk MCP tools and access to the relevant survey account.
Account connections, revoked credentials, and external service permissions require user action outside the chat.
Bitrix24 lacks a dedicated delivery log in this workflow; its connectivity check does not confirm every lead arrived.
Retries cover supported messenger and webhook operations; successful downstream delivery depends on the receiving service.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing CRM Leads
use_cases.description: Check survey integration status and Bitrix24 connectivity, then identify the account repair needed to restore access.

use_cases.title: Restore Team Notifications
use_cases.description: Review Telegram or MAX delivery failures, explain the required chat repair, and retry failed notifications after recovery.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Webhook Delivery Errors
use_cases.description: Inspect webhook status and receiver response codes, then retry a failed delivery after the endpoint is repaired.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Missing Notification
prompt_templates.prompt: Telegram notifications stopped for the survey named [survey name]. Confirm the survey and explain the cause without changing settings.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate CRM Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Check why survey [survey ID] no longer sends leads to Bitrix24. Inspect integration status and portal connectivity, then explain any required account repairs.

prompt_templates.title: Recover Failed Messenger Deliveries
prompt_templates.prompt: For survey [survey ID], verify that the Telegram failure is resolved. Retry failed notifications from [start date] to [end date] and report the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recover a defined batch after repair.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Multiple Delivery Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit survey [survey ID] across CRM, Google Sheets, messengers, and webhooks. Separate configuration issues from receiver failures. Propose repairs without changing settings or replaying deliveries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate diagnosis across multiple integrations.

output_examples.input: Example scenario: Telegram logs show that the bot was removed from the group.
output: Cause: the bot is no longer a member of the destination group.
Required action: return the bot to the group.
Retry status: no deliveries retried while the cause remains unresolved.

output_examples.input: Example scenario: the webhook delivery log shows an HTTP 500 response.
output: Cause: the receiving endpoint returned a server error.
Required action: investigate and repair the receiving service before retrying the failed delivery.
Secret handling: keep masked authorization headers unchanged.

output_examples.input: Example scenario: the CRM integration is blocked by the current plan.
output: Cause: the integration is unavailable under the current plan.
Result: diagnosis stopped without changing settings or retrying delivery.

best_practices: Confirm the survey identity and inspect integration status before running deeper checks.
Resolve the underlying service failure before retrying a clearly scoped set of deliveries.
Obtain consent before enabling delivery and keep masked webhook credentials out of chat.
anti_patterns: Enabling a disabled integration without checking whether it was intentionally paused.
Repeating failed deliveries before repairing the underlying cause.
Requesting secret header values or overwriting webhook configuration merely to test access.

faq.question: What must be configured before using this skill?
faq.answer: Your assistant needs the WebAsk MCP tools and authorized access to the survey. The skill provides instructions, not the MCP server implementation.

faq.question: Which integrations does the workflow cover?
faq.answer: It covers Telegram, MAX, Bitrix24, Google Sheets, and webhooks, with different checks for each service.

faq.question: Can it connect an account or restore revoked credentials?
faq.answer: No. It explains the required repair, but account connections and credential recovery must happen in the relevant service dashboard.

faq.question: Will it automatically enable a disabled integration?
faq.answer: No. The workflow asks whether delivery was disabled intentionally and requires consent before enabling it.

faq.question: When can failed deliveries be retried?
faq.answer: After the underlying problem is resolved, it can retry supported messenger deliveries and individual webhook deliveries.

faq.question: Does troubleshooting require sharing webhook secrets?
faq.answer: No. The workflow treats masked header values as secrets and prohibits requesting them or overwriting headers for testing.
